name: GukiZ and Binary Operations
description: We all know that GukiZ often plays with arrays. Now he is thinking about this problem: how many arrays a , of length n , with non-negative elements strictly less then 2 l meet the following condition: ? Here operation means bitwise AND (in Pascal it is equivalent to and , in C/C++/Java/Python it is equivalent to & ), operation means bitwise OR (in Pascal it is equivalent to , in C/C++/Java/Python it is equivalent to | ). Because the answer can be quite large, calculate it modulo m . This time GukiZ hasn't come up with solution, and needs you to help him!
input_specification: First and the only line of input contains four integers n , k , l , m ( 2 ≤ n ≤ 10 18 , 0 ≤ k ≤ 10 18 , 0 ≤ l ≤ 64 , 1 ≤ m ≤ 10 9 + 7 ).
output_specification: In the single line print the number of arrays satisfying the condition above modulo m .
approach_summary: Formulate linear recurrence as state transition vector V_{n+1} = M * V_n. Compute M^K via binary matrix exponentiation in O(D^3 log K) time.
